claim: Fibroblastic cells were isolated from seven PDAC surgical specimens obtained from five different individuals.
source: Fibroblasts were isolated from seven PDAC surgical specimens obtained from five different individuals (with four specimens reflecting two matched tumor-normal pairs, one tumor specimen lacking a matched normal control, and two specimens pathologically designated as non-tumor/normal).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number and source of specimens used.

claim: Fibroblasts were characterized as naïve pancreatic stellate cells or PDAC-associated desmoplastic CAFs based on mRNA and protein expression of palladin and αSMA.
source: These fibroblasts were characterized as naïve pancreatic stellate cells or PDAC-associated desmoplastic CAFs on the basis of assessments of the mRNA and protein expression of the myofibroblastic markers palladin and αSMA (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: The manuscript describes the characterization method using specific markers.

claim: Desmoplastic CAFs produced anisotropic D-ECM with multi-layered myofibroblastic spindled nuclei and increased levels of stress fiber-localized αSMA.
source: Desmoplastic CAFs produced anisotropic D-ECM with multi-layered myofibroblastic spindled nuclei and increased levels of stress fiber-localized αSMA reminiscent of myofibroblastic cells in vivo (Goetz et al., 2011; Provenzano et al., 2006; Conklin et al., 2011; Eyden, 2001; Kalluri and Zeisberg, 2006), whereas fibroblasts derived from normal specimens did not (Figure 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes observed characteristics of CAF-produced ECM and cites supporting literature.

claim: An arbitrary quantitative threshold of at least 55% of fibers oriented at a spread of 15° from the mode angle was used to indicate D-ECMs produced by activated CAFs.
source: We used an arbitrary quantitative threshold of at least 55% of fibers oriented at a spread of 15° from the mode angle as indicative of D-ECMs that had been produced by activated CAFs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the threshold used for classification.

claim: Levels of TGFβ in D-ECM were approximately 2-fold higher than in N-ECM or D-ECM produced in the presence of SB-431542.
source: Levels of TGFβ in D-ECM were ~2 fold higher than in N-ECM or D-ECM produced in the presence of SB-431542 (D+TGFβi in Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative ELISA measurements comparing TGFβ levels.

claim: Following SB-431542 treatment, CAFs produced isotropic ECMs that were phenotypically indistinguishable from intact N-ECMs.
source: Importantly, following SB-431542 treatment, CAFs produced isotropic ECMs that were phenotypically indistinguishable from intact N-ECMs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–D).
evidence: The manuscript describes the phenotypic outcome of TGFβ inhibition during ECM production.

claim: Treatment of control naïve pancreatic stellate cells with SB-431542 caused complete loss of fibrillogenesis, resulting in the absence of matrix production.
source: This result differed from that produced by the treatment of control naïve pancreatic stellate cells with SB-431542, which produced interrupted TGFβ signaling that caused complete loss of fibrillogenesis, resulting in the absence of matrix production (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript describes the differential effect of TGFβ inhibition on naïve cells versus CAFs.

claim: The increased TGFβ observed in D-ECM was critical for CAF production of anisotropic matrices.
source: Together, these results suggested that the increased TGFβ observed in D-ECM was critical for CAF production of anisotropic matrices.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion from the experimental results regarding TGFβ's role.

claim: D-ECM produced by CAFs in the presence of TGFβ blockade was incapable of inducing de novo myofibroblastic activation in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells.
source: Applying this analysis to pancreatic extracted matrices, we found that D-ECM produced by CAFs in the presence of TGFβ blockade was similar to N-ECM in being incapable of inducing de novo myofibroblastic activation (as reflected by increased αSMA stress fiber localization and protein levels) in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental findings on the functional capacity of TGFβ-inhibited D-ECM.

claim: Untreated and control treated D-ECM effectively induced myofibroblastic activation in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells.
source: By contrast,untreated and control treated D-ECM effectively induced such activation (Figure 2, Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the contrasting effect of untreated D-ECM.

claim: Myofibroblastic activation is a general phenomenon during interactions between naïve pancreatic stellate cells and CAF-produced PDAC-associated D-ECMs across all five PDAC patients.
source: Similar results were obtained using D-ECM and naïve fibroblastic stellate cells for all five PDAC patients (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Table 2), suggesting that myofibroblastic activation is a general phenomenon during interactions between naïve pancreatic stellate cells and CAF-produced PDAC-associated D-ECMs.
evidence: The manuscript generalizes findings across multiple patient samples.

claim: αSMA mRNA levels were comparable in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells cultured in N- vs D-ECM.
source: A post-translational effect was implied by the fact that αSMA mRNA levels were comparable in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells cultured in N- vs D-ECM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: The manuscript reports RT-qPCR measurements showing no difference in mRNA levels.

claim: Use of cycloheximide to inhibit protein translation did not alter αSMA expression levels.
source: and because use of cycloheximide to inhibit protein translation did not alter αSMA expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results using a translation inhibitor.

claim: Growth of naïve stellate cells in the presence of SB-431542 did not block D-ECM-induced αSMA expression or localization to stress fibers.
source: Growth of these cells in the presence of SB-431542 did not block D-ECM-induced αSMA expression or localization to stress fibers.
evidence: The manuscript reports that TGFβ inhibition during naïve cell culture does not prevent activation.

claim: TGFβ inhibition during D-ECM production reduces the ability of CAFs to produce ECM that can induce myofibroblastic activation.
source: Together, these results suggested that TGFβ inhibition during D-ECM production reduces the ability of CAFs to produce ECM that can induce myofibroblastic activation
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: Once D-ECM has been deposited by CAFs, TGFβ retained within the D-ECM is subsequently dispensable for D-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation of naïve stellate cells.
source: but that once D-ECM has been deposited by CAFs, TGFβ retained within the D-ECM is subsequently dispensable for D-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation of naïve stellate cells.
evidence: The manuscript concludes that TGFβ is not required after ECM deposition.

claim: Integrins αvβ5 and α5β1 have been reported to participate in myofibroblastic activation.
source: Integrins αvβ5 and α5β1 have been reported to participate in myofibroblastic activation (Asano et al., 2006; Lygoe et al., 2004; Dugina et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior literature on integrin involvement.

claim: Both αvβ5 and α5β1 integrin heterodimers were highly abundant on the plasma membranes of human naïve pancreatic stellate cells and PDAC-associated CAFs.
source: We first established that both of these integrin heterodimers were highly abundant, compared to other β-integrins, on the PMs of human naïve pancreatic stellate cells and of PDAC-associated CAFs (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from an integrin-dependent cell adhesion array.

claim: ALULA, a highly specific αvβ5-integrin-blocking antibody, eliminated the ability of D-ECM to induce αSMA stress fiber localization beyond levels induced by N-ECM.
source: ALULA, a highly specific αvβ5-integrin-blocking antibody (Su et al., 2007), eliminated the ability of D-ECM to induce αSMA stress fiber localization (and expression) beyond levels induced by N-ECM (Figure 3B–E and Table 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results using a blocking antibody.

claim: mAb16, which specifically blocks human α5β1-integrin activity, had limited effects on D-ECM induction of αSMA localization.
source: By contrast, mAb16, which specifically blocks human α5β1-integrin activity (Akiyama et al., 1989), had limited effects on D-ECM induction of αSMA localization (or expression), with naïve cells undergoing robust myofibroblastic conversion (Figure 3B–E and Table 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results using a different blocking antibody.

claim: Combined application of ALULA and mAb16 eliminated the effects of αvβ5-integrin inhibition seen with ALULA alone, with naïve cells undergoing robust myofibroblastic transition.
source: Intriguingly, combined application of ALULA and mAb16 eliminated the effects of αvβ5-integrin inhibition seen with ALULA alone, with naïve cells undergoing robust myofibroblastic transition similar to that in untreated and IgG controls (Figure 3B–E and Table 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports the unexpected result of combined integrin inhibition.

claim: SNAKA51, an activating antibody that stabilizes the active conformation of α5β1-integrin, reduced the ability of D-ECM to induce αSMA stress fiber localization in naïve stellate cells.
source: We found that SNAKA51, an activating antibody that stabilizes the active conformation of α5β1-integrin (Clark et al., 2005), reduced the ability of D-ECM to induce αSMA stress fiber localization (and expression) in naïve stellate cells (Figure 3 and Table 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results using an activating antibody.

claim: Naïve stellate cells lacking the β5 integrin subunit had a greatly diminished response to D-ECM, with very limited induction of αSMA stress fiber localization.
source: Cells lacking the β5 subunit had a greatly diminished response to D-ECM, with very limited induction of αSMA stress fiber localization (and expression) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from CRISPR-edited cells lacking β5 integrin.

claim: Loss of α5-, αv- or β3-integrin profoundly reduced growth of naïve fibroblasts, yielding slow-growing cells that were also unable to respond to D-ECM.
source: By contrast, loss of α5-, αv- or β3-integrin profoundly reduced growth of naïve fibroblasts, yielding slow-growing cells that were also unable to respond to D-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript reports the phenotype of cells lacking other integrin subunits.

claim: Neither αvβ5-integrin inhibition nor stabilization of active α5β1-integrin altered the anisotropic fiber formation in D-ECM deposited by CAFs.
source: In contrast to results with TGFβ blockade, neither αvβ5-integrin inhibition (with ALULA) nor stabilization of active α5β1-integrin (with SNAKA51) altered the anisotropic fiber formation in D-ECM deposited by CAFs (Figure 4)
evidence: The manuscript reports that integrin manipulation during ECM production does not affect anisotropy.

claim: Neither αvβ5-integrin inhibition nor stabilization of active α5β1-integrin altered the ability of CAF-produced matrices to induce myofibroblastic activation in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells.
source: or the ability of these matrices to induce myofibroblastic activation in naïve fibroblastic stellate cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports that integrin manipulation during ECM production does not affect ECM function.

claim: CAFs lacking β5-integrin subunits had decreased αSMA expression and localization of αSMA to stress fibers.
source: In contrast to results with integrin inhibition, CAFs lacking β5-integrin or α5-integrin subunits had decreased αSMA expression and localization of αSMA to stress fibers.
evidence: The manuscript reports the phenotype of CRISPR-edited CAFs.

claim: Loss of β5 expression in CAFs affected levels of D-ECM anisotropy.
source: Loss of β5 expression also affected levels of D-ECM anisotropy
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of β5 loss on ECM organization.

claim: CAFs lacking α5 failed to produce substantial matrices.
source: while CAFs lacking α5 failed to produce substantial matrices (matching earlier reports [Pankov et al., 2000; McDonald et al., 1987; Fogerty et al., 1990]) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of α5 loss on ECM production and cites supporting literature.

claim: Loss of αv-integrin caused significant reduction in the ability to produce D-ECM.
source: In addition, loss of αv-integrin caused significant reduction in the ability to produce D-ECM
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αv loss on ECM production.

claim: Loss of β3 integrin had no effect on D-ECM production phenotype.
source: while loss of the negative control, β3, had no effect on this phenotype (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript reports that β3 loss does not affect ECM production.

claim: The requirement for specific integrins in the response of naïve fibroblastic cells to D-ECMs differs from the requirement for integrins during CAF production of anisotropic D-ECMs.
source: Together, these data indicated that the requirement for specific integrins in the response of naïve fibroblastic cells to D-ECMs differs from the requirement for integrins during CAF production of anisotropic D-ECMs.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion comparing integrin requirements in different contexts.

claim: FAK inhibition strongly reduced the ability of naïve fibroblastic stellate cells plated in D-ECM to acquire myofibroblastic traits.
source: FAK inhibition strongly reduced the ability of these cells to acquire myofibroblastic traits, similar to the result seen with αvβ5-integrin inhibition (Figure 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results using a FAK inhibitor.

claim: Naïve pancreatic stellate cells treated concomitantly with PF573,228 and mAb16 underwent myofibroblastic conversion, re-localizing and upregulating αSMA.
source: Further, naïve pancreatic stellate cells treated concomitantly with PF573,228 and the α5β1-integrin-inhibiting mAb16 (Akiyama et al., 1989) underwent a myofibroblastic conversion, re-localizing and upregulating αSMA (Figure 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports the result of combined FAK and α5β1 inhibition.

claim: Treatment of naïve murine fibroblasts plated in mD-ECM with PF573,228 blocked acquisition of myofibroblastic traits.
source: Emphasizing a general mechanism, treatment of naïve murine fibroblasts plated in mD-ECM with PF573,228 blocked acquisition of myofibroblastic traits (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports that the FAK inhibition effect is conserved in a murine model.

claim: In naïve murine fibroblasts, concomitant FAK and α5β1-integrin inhibition significantly increased mD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic conversion compared with PF573,228 treatment alone.
source: In naïve murine fibroblasts, concomitant FAK and α5β1-integrin inhibition with combined PF573,228 and BMA5 significantly increased mD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic conversion when compared with PF573,228 treatment alone
evidence: The manuscript reports the result of combined inhibition in murine cells.

claim: αvβ5-integrin co-inhibition with FAK did not increase mD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic conversion in naïve murine fibroblasts.
source: while αvβ5-integrin co-inhibition with FAK did not (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the differential effect of αvβ5 versus α5β1 co-inhibition with FAK.

claim: FAK-/- murine naïve fibroblastic cells grown in mD-ECM had greatly reduced myofibroblastic activation, which was significantly increased if α5β1 but not αvβ5 integrin activation was blocked.
source: Further, FAK-/- murine naïve fibroblastic cells (Ilić et al., 1995) grown in mD-ECM had greatly reduced myofibroblastic activation, which was significantly increased if α5β1 but not αvβ5 integrin activation was blocked (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from FAK knockout cells.

claim: Murine fibroblasts overexpressing FAK-KD displayed a lack of myofibroblastic response to mD-ECM compared to control cells, and α5β1-integrin inhibition rescued this phenotype.
source: Immortalized murine fibroblasts overexpressing FAK-KD displayed a lack of myofibroblastic response to mD-ECM compared to the response seen in isogenic hTert immortalized control cells, and again, an efficient rescue of this phenotype was imparted by α5β1-integrin inhibition (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from cells expressing dominant negative FAK.

claim: Fibroblasts null for SRC family kinases SRC, FYN and YES were unable to respond to mD-ECM, and inhibition of α5β1-integrin did not restore the mD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic phenotype.
source: We found that the ablation of SRC family kinases also negated the ability of fibroblasts to respond to mD-ECM. Interestingly, in this context, inhibition of α5β1-integrin did not restore the mD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic phenotype, indicating non-equivalent functions of FAK and SRC (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from SRC family kinase knockout cells.

claim: The ability of the FAK inhibitor to block D-ECM-induced myofibroblastic transition depended on an intact α5β1 heterodimer.
source: Last, we explored the relationship between FAK and α5-integrin expression (as opposed to integrin activity). The ability of the FAK inhibitor to block D-ECM-induced myofibroblastic transition depended on an intact α5β1 heterodimer, as PF573,228 did not rescue the mD-ECM-induced process that was disrupted in α5-KO naïve stellate cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports that FAK inhibition requires α5β1 expression.

claim: FAK is essential for D-ECM-induced myofibroblast activation, but dispensable for the α5β1-integrin inhibition of this process.
source: Together, these results suggested that FAK is essential for D-ECM-induced myofibroblast activation, but dispensable for the α5β1-integrin inhibition of this process.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion about FAK's role from the experimental results.

claim: Genetic ablation of α5β1-integrin does not recapitulate the result of inhibition of integrin activity in D-ECM responsiveness.
source: The data further indicate that genetic ablation of α5β1-integrin does not recapitulate the result of inhibition of integrin activity in D-ECM responsiveness, perhaps due to additional functional requirements for this integrin in supporting fundamental cell growth.
evidence: The manuscript notes a difference between genetic deletion and functional inhibition.

claim: Naïve stellate cells cultured within D-ECM typically increased the length of 3D-adhesions by approximately 14% compared to adhesions formed in N-ECM.
source: Naïve stellate cells cultured within D-ECM typically increased the length of 3D-adhesions by ~14% compared to adhesions formed in N-ECM (Figure 6).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative measurements of adhesion length.

claim: Stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity using SNAKA51 eliminated the ability of D-ECM to induce 3D-adhesion lengthening.
source: While inhibition of α5β1-integrin with mAb16 was previously shown to cause 3D-adhesion loss (Cukierman et al., 2001), stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity using SNAKA51 eliminated the ability of D-ECM to induce 3D-adhesion lengthening.
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of α5β1 stabilization on adhesion length.

claim: αvβ5-integrin inhibition with ALULA did not prevent D-ECM-induced 3D-adhesion lengthening.
source: However, αvβ5-integrin inhibition with ALULA did not (Figure 6).
evidence: The manuscript reports that αvβ5 inhibition does not affect adhesion lengthening.

claim: Plating of naïve stellate cells in D-ECM induced a 4-fold increase in active α5β1-integrin levels compared to plating in N-ECM.
source: Plating of naïve stellate cells in D-ECM induced a 4-fold increase in active α5β1-integrin levels compared to plating in N-ECM (Figure 6—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative measurements of active integrin levels.

claim: The increase in active α5β1-integrin did not reflect an increase in α5β1 localized to 3D adhesions but rather a concentration in membrane-proximal regions lacking adhesions.
source: but surprisingly, this did not reflect an increase in α5β1 localized to 3D adhesions (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) but rather a concentration (~2 fold) in membrane-proximal regions areas lacking adhesions.
evidence: The manuscript reports the spatial distribution of active integrin.

claim: D-ECM induced approximately 2-fold more pFAK-Y397 than N-ECM, and this activated FAK was localized at 3D-adhesions.
source: Results normalized to levels obtained in D-ECMs (a.u. = 1.0) indicated that D-ECM induced ~2 fold more pFAK-Y397 than N-ECM, and that this activated FAK was localized at 3D-adhesions (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative measurements of pFAK localization.

claim: If fibroblasts are cultured in the presence of αvβ5-integrin inhibitor ALULA, significantly lower levels of pFAK-Y397 at 3D-adhesions and active α5β1-integrin away from 3D-adhesions were observed in cells cultured within D-ECM.
source: By contrast, if fibroblasts are cultured in the presence of the αvβ5-integrin inhibitor ALULA, significantly lower levels of pFAK-Y397 at 3D-adhesions and active α5β1-integrin away from 3D-adhesions were observed in cells cultured within D-ECM (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αvβ5 inhibition on pFAK and active integrin distribution.

claim: Non-permeabilized cells had a 5-fold reduction of detectable D-ECM-induced active α5β1-integrin relative to permeabilized cells.
source: Non-permeabilized cells had a 5-fold reduction of detectable D-ECM-induced active (SNAKA51-positive) α5β1-integrin relative to permeabilized cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4), indicating that the activated integrin may be rapidly internalized.
evidence: The manuscript reports results from permeabilization experiments indicating intracellular localization.

claim: Inhibition of αvβ5-integrin by treatment with ALULA effectively eliminated the intracellular pool of active α5β1-integrin while considerably increasing the amounts of surface-exposed active α5β1-integrin induced by growth in D-ECM.
source: In addition, inhibition of αvβ5-integrin, by treatment with ALULA, effectively eliminated the intracellular pool while it considerably increased the amounts of surface-exposed active α5β1-integrin induced by growth in D-ECM (Figure 6—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αvβ5 inhibition on integrin localization.

claim: Naïve β5-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells plated within D-ECM had 2.7- and 2.5-fold decreases in total α5β1-integrin activity and pFAK-Y397 levels, respectively, when compared to control KO cells.
source: Naïve β5-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells plated within D-ECM had 2.7- and 2.5-fold decreases in total α5β1-integrin activity and pFAK-Y397 levels, respectively, when compared to control KO cells (Figure 7).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative measurements from β5 knockout cells.

claim: No detectable α5β1-integrin activity was observed in α5-KO naïve stellate cells.
source: As expected, no detectable α5β1-integrin activity was observed in α5-KO
evidence: The manuscript reports the expected result from α5 knockout cells.

claim: Only modest decreases in the activity of α5β1-integrin were observed in αv and β3-integrin KO cells grown in intact D-ECM.
source: while only modest decreases in the activity of α5β1-integrin was observed in αv and β3-integrin KO cells grown in intact D-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of other integrin knockouts on α5β1 activity.

claim: A modest pFAK-Y397 downregulation was observed in α5-KO cells.
source: Interestingly, while a modest pFAK-Y397 downregulation was observed in α5-KO
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of α5 knockout on pFAK levels.

claim: There were no appreciable changes in pFAK-Y397 in αv-KO cells.
source: there were no appreciable changes in pFAK-Y397 in αv-KO cells
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αv knockout on pFAK levels.

claim: A small increase in pFAK-Y397 was induced by D-ECM in β3-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells.
source: whereas a small increase in pFAK-Y397 was induced by D-ECM in β3-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of β3 knockout on pFAK levels.

claim: β5-integrin was an effective regulator of both active α5β1-integrin and pFAK-Y397 levels in the response of naïve stellate cells to D-ECM.
source: Although results with αv- and β3-integrin KO did not exclude these integrins from any role in response to D-ECM, these experiments indicated that β5-integrin was an effective regulator of both active α5β1-integrin and pFAK-Y397 levels in the response of naïve stellate cells to D-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion about β5's regulatory role from the knockout experiments.

claim: SNAKA51 stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity reduced intracellular, while increasing PM, pools of active α5β1-integrin when compared to a non-specific IgG treatment control.
source: SNAKA51 stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity reduced intracellular, while increasing PM, pools of active α5β1-integrin when compared to a non-specific IgG treatment control (Figure 8A).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of SNAKA51 on integrin localization.

claim: D-ECM induced the intracellular enrichment of active integrin in discrete punctate structures, which probably reflected endosomes that did not include recognizable clathrin-coated pits.
source: D-ECM induced the intracellular enrichment of the active integrin in discrete punctate structures, which probably reflected endosomes that did not include recognizable clathrin-coated pits.
evidence: The manuscript reports electron microscopy observations and interprets the structures.

claim: Inhibition of αvβ5-integrin reduced the accumulation of active α5β1-integrin intracellular pools, with most signal localized to the PM.
source: Conversely, inhibition of αvβ5-integrin reduced the accumulation of active α5β1-integrin intracellular pools, with most signal localized to the PM (Figure 8B).
evidence: The manuscript reports electron microscopy observations of αvβ5 inhibition effects.

claim: The relocation of active α5β1-integrin from intracellular to PM locations following culture within intact D-ECM was also observed in naïve β5-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells compared to control naïve fibroblasts.
source: Supporting this mechanism in an independent model, the relocation of active α5β1-integrin from intracellular to PM locations following culture within intact D-ECM was also observed in naïve β5-integrin KO fibroblastic stellate cells that were compared to control naïve fibroblasts (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports electron microscopy observations from β5 knockout cells.

claim: D-ECM induced the partial localization of active α5β1-integrin to Rab7-, Rab11-, and most clearly, to CD81-positive endosomes in control KO fibroblasts.
source: D-ECM induced the partial localization of active α5β1-integrin to Rab7-, Rab11-, and most clearly, to CD81-positive endosomes in control KO fibroblasts (Figure 9).
evidence: The manuscript reports immunofluorescence colocalization results.

claim: β5-KO naïve fibroblasts did not similarly relocalize active α5β1-integrin to intracellular locations following plating in D-ECM.
source: By contrast, β5-KO naïve fibroblasts did not similarly relocalize active α5β1-integrin to these intracellular locations following plating in D-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript reports the absence of relocalization in β5 knockout cells.

claim: β5-integrin KO CAFs had no discernible differences in levels of active α5β1-integrin when compared to control KO CAFs.
source: β5-integrin KO CAFs, which have deficiencies in myofibroblastic expression of αSMA and in the formation of anisotropic D-ECM (see Figure 4—figure supplement 2), had no discernible differences in levels of active α5β1-integrin when compared to control KO CAFs.
evidence: The manuscript reports that β5 knockout in CAFs does not affect active α5β1 levels.

claim: β5-integrin KO CAFs had notable downregulation of pFAK-Y397 expression.
source: However, β5-integrin KO CAFs cells had notable downregulation of pFAK-Y397 expression, suggesting a disturbance in overall integrin signaling that resulted from the loss of this cell-matrix receptor (Figure 10).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of β5 knockout on pFAK in CAFs.

claim: A specific mechanistic decoupling between myofibroblastic features and the regulation of active α5β1-integrin in CAFs was observed in the analysis of β5-integrin KO CAFs.
source: In contrast to the observed concomitant regulation of stress-fiber-localized αSMA and of the increased active levels of α5β1-integrin and FAK in naïve fibroblastic cells responding to D-ECM, a specific mechanistic decoupling between myofibroblastic features, such as αSMA expression and anisotropic D-ECM production, and the regulation of active α5β1-integrin in CAFs was observed in this analysis of β5-integrin KO CAFs.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion about mechanistic differences between naïve cells and CAFs.

claim: Loss of αv-integrin in CAFs led to failure to produce 3D ECMs and to low αSMA expression, but did not affect levels of active α5β1-integrin.
source: Loss of αv-integrin in CAFs, which led to failure to produce 3D ECMs and to low αSMA expression, did not affect levels of active α5β1-integrin
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αv knockout in CAFs.

claim: Loss of the β3-integrin subunit in CAFs, which is associated with cells competent for induction of myofibroblastic features, significantly lowered active α5β1-integrin levels.
source: whereas loss of the β3-integrin subunit, which is associated with cells competent for induction of myofibroblastic features, significantly lowered active α5β1-integrin levels (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of β3 knockout in CAFs.

claim: The requirement in CAFs for αvβ5 integrin expression during the concomitant regulation of αSMA levels and anisotropic D-ECM production differs from the dispensable nature of αvβ5 for the maintenance of high active α5β1-integrin levels in these cells.
source: The observed differences between the requirement in CAFs for αvβ5 integrin expression during the concomitant regulation of αSMA levels and anisotropic D-ECM production, versus the dispensable nature of αvβ5 for the maintenance of high active α5β1-integrin levels in these cells, suggests a functional decoupling between the processes.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion about functional decoupling in CAFs.

claim: Renal fibroblasts include an overrepresentation of α5β1 and αvβ5 integrins relative to alternative β-integrin heterodimers at the plasma membrane.
source: We first demonstrated that renal (r) fibroblasts include an overrepresentation of α5β1 and αvβ5 integrins relative to alternative β-integrin heterodimers at the plasma membrane (Figure 11A).
evidence: The manuscript reports integrin expression in renal fibroblasts.

claim: Naïve r-fibroblasts expressed low levels of αSMA.
source: Naïve r-fibroblasts expressed low levels of αSMA (Figure 11B–C)
evidence: The manuscript reports αSMA expression in naïve renal fibroblasts.

claim: Naïve r-fibroblasts produced isotropic rN-ECM when compared to rCAF-derived matrices, which produced anisotropic rD-ECM.
source: and produced isotropic rN-ECM when compared to rCAF-derived matrices, which produced anisotropic rD-ECM (Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports ECM organization in renal fibroblast cultures.

claim: Treating rCAFs with TGFβ inhibitor during ECM production caused cells to produce isotropic matrices.
source: As with PDAC CAFs, treating rCAFs with a TGFβ inhibitor (SB-431542) during ECM production caused cells to produce isotropic matrices (Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of TGFβ inhibition in renal CAFs.

claim: Overnight plating of naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM induced the formation of myofibroblastic features such as an increase in stress-fiber-localized αSMA, as compared to cells plated in rN-ECM.
source: Overnight plating of naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM induced the formation of myofibroblastic features such as an increase in stress-fiber-localized αSMA, as compared to cells plated in rN-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of rD-ECM on naïve renal fibroblasts.

claim: The isotropic 3D matrices produced by TGFβR1-inhibited rCAFs failed to induce naïve-to-myofibroblastic activation.
source: Further, the isotropic 3D matrices produced by TGFβR1-inhibited rCAFs failed to induce naïve-to-myofibroblastic activation
evidence: The manuscript reports that TGFβ-inhibited rD-ECM is not functional.

claim: TGFβ signaling activity was dispensable in naïve fibroblasts undergoing myofibroblastic activation in response to intact rD-ECM induction.
source: whereas TGFβ signaling activity was dispensable in naïve fibroblasts undergoing myofibroblastic activation in response to intact rD-ECM induction.
evidence: The manuscript reports that TGFβ is not required in naïve cells responding to rD-ECM.

claim: Regulation of active α5β1-integrin by αvβ5-integrin was needed for naïve fibroblasts to undergo rD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation.
source: In addition, as with the pancreatic model, regulation of active α5β1-integrin by αvβ5-integrin was needed for naïve fibroblasts to undergo rD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation (Figure 11—figure supplement 2 and Table 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports that the integrin mechanism is conserved in renal fibroblasts.

claim: Treatment of naïve r-fibroblasts seeded within rD-ECM in the presence of FAK inhibitor PF573,228 blocked acquisition of myofibroblastic traits.
source: Accordingly, treatment of naïve r-fibroblasts seeded within rD-ECM in the presence of small molecule FAK inhibitor PF573,228 (Slack-Davis et al., 2007), blocked acquisition of myofibroblastic traits (Figure 11—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of FAK inhibition in renal fibroblasts.

claim: In naïve r-fibroblasts, concomitant FAK and α5β1-integrin inhibition significantly increased rD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation compared to PF573,228 treatment alone.
source: In naïve r-fibroblasts, concomitant FAK and α5β1-integrin inhibition with combined PF573,228 and mAb16 significantly increased rD-ECM-induced myofibroblastic activation compared to PF573,228 treatment alone.
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of combined inhibition in renal fibroblasts.

claim: αvβ5-integrin co-inhibition with FAK failed to rescue rD-ECM naïve-to-myofibroblastic conversion.
source: Again, effects similar to those observed in the PDAC system were seen: αvβ5-integrin co-inhibition with FAK failed to rescue rD-ECM naïve-to-myofibroblastic conversion (Figure 11—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript reports that the FAK-integrin interaction is conserved in renal fibroblasts.

claim: pFAK-Y397 levels measured in 3D-adhesions of naïve r-fibroblasts induced by rD-ECM were effectively reduced in the presence of αVβ5-integrin inhibitor.
source: Also, pFAK-Y397 levels measured in 3D-adhesions of naïve r-fibroblasts induced by rD-ECM were effectively reduced in the presence of αVβ5-integrin inhibitor (ALULA [Su et al., 2007]), rendering pFAK-Y397 levels similar to N-ECM levels (Figure 11—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αvβ5 inhibition on pFAK in renal fibroblasts.

claim: Culturing naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM triggered lengthening of 3D-adhesion structures compared to those in rN-ECM, and this was effectively prevented by stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity using SNAKA51.
source: Culturing naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM triggered lengthening of 3D-adhesion structures compared to those in rN-ECM, and this was effectively prevented by stabilization of α5β1-integrin activity using SNAKA51 (Clark et al., 2005) (Figure 11—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of rD-ECM and α5β1 stabilization on adhesion length in renal fibroblasts.

claim: Plating naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM increased levels of active α5β1-integrin that was localized away from 3D-adhesion structures compared to those in rN-ECM.
source: Last, plating naïve r-fibroblasts in rD-ECM increased levels of active α5β1-integrin that was localized away from 3D-adhesion structures compared to those in rN-ECM.
evidence: The manuscript reports the spatial distribution of active integrin in renal fibroblasts.

claim: These levels of active α5β1-integrin were regulated by αvβ5-integrin, as treatment with ALULA restricted the enrichment of α5β1-integrin activity in areas lacking adhesions.
source: These levels were regulated by αvβ5-integrin, as treatment with ALULA restricted the enrichment of α5β1-integrin activity in areas lacking adhesions (Figure 11—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript reports the effect of αvβ5 inhibition on integrin distribution in renal fibroblasts.

claim: The mechanisms identified for PDAC D-ECM production and activity were also relevant in RCC-associated fibroblastic stroma.
source: Together, these results imply that the mechanisms identified for PDAC D-ECM production and activity were also relevant in RCC-associated fibroblastic stroma.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion about the generalizability of the findings.

claim: During D-ECM production in vitro, CAFs maintain high levels of active α5β1-integrin, with much of the active pool not localized to 3D-adhesions, as well as high levels of pFAK-Y397 that are localized at 3D-adhesions.
source: This method reiterated our observation that during D-ECM production in vitro, CAFs maintain high levels of active α5β1-integrin, with much of the active pool not localized to 3D-adhesions, as well as high levels of pFAK-Y397 that are localized at 3D-adhesions.
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from the SMI approach in vitro.

claim: TGFβ activation increased during the production of D-ECM, represented by augmented total and nuclear pSMAD2/3 levels, when compared to naïve/normal cultures.
source: TGFβ activation also increased during the production of D-ECM, represented by augmented total and nuclear pSMAD2/3 levels, when compared to naïve/normal cultures in which active α5β1-integrin mostly localizes at 3D-adhesion sites during N-ECM matrix production (Figure 12).
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from the SMI approach in vitro.

claim: Normal pancreatic and renal 3D cultures included active α5β1-integrin that is mostly localized at 3D-adhesion locations and included relatively low pFAK and pSMAD2/3 levels.
source: While normal pancreatic and renal 3D cultures included active α5β1-integrin that is mostly localized at 3D-adhesion locations and included relatively low pFAK and pSMAD2/3 levels
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from indirect immunofluorescence in vitro.

claim: PDAC and RCC CAF 3D matrix-producing cultures exhibited high active α5β1-integrin levels that were evident at locations away from 3D-adhesions, concomitant with increased pFAK-Y397, and nuclei that were enriched with pSMAD2/3.
source: PDAC and RCC CAF 3D matrix-producing cultures again exhibited high active α5β1-integrin levels that were evident at locations away from 3D-adhesions, concomitant with increased pFAK-Y397, and nuclei that were enriched with pSMAD2/3 (Figure 12—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from indirect immunofluorescence in vitro.

claim: Analysis of FFPE samples indicated clear increases in total α5β1-integrin activity, pFAK-Y397, and pSMAD2/3 in the stroma of PDAC and RCC compared to normal pancreatic and renal parenchyma.
source: This analysis indicated clear increases in total α5β1-integrin activity, pFAK-Y397, and pSMAD2/3 in the stroma of PDAC and RCC compared to normal pancreatic and renal parenchyma (Figure 12—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from FFPE tissue analysis.

claim: When the same comparisons were performed for α5β1-integrin activity specifically localized away from stromal 3D-adhesion-positive pixels, the results again indicated clear increases.
source: When the same comparisons were performed for α5β1-integrin activity specifically localized away from stromal 3D-adhesion-positive pixels, the results again indicated clear increases (Figure 12—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The manuscript reports observations from FFPE tissue analysis.

claim: For PDAC specimens, association between pathological N stage, overall pathological stage and positive nodes with overall survival indicated a significant increased risk of death correlated with increasing levels of these variables.
source: For PDAC specimens, association between pathological N stage , overall pathological stage and positive nodes with overall survival (OS) indicated a significant increased risk of death correlated with increasing levels of these variables, with Uni hazard ratios (HRs) of 2.5 for pathological N (p=0.0002; 95% CI 1.5–4.2), 1.3 for pathological stage (p=0.01; 95% CI 1.1–1.6) and 1.15 for positive nodes (p=0.0001; 95% CI 1.1–1.2).
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical analysis of clinical variables.

claim: Similar analyses looking at the association between clinical variables and recurrence-free survival resulted in the identification of positive correlations for pathological N, pathological stage and positive nodes.
source: Similar analyses looking at the association between clinical variables and recurrence-free survival (RFS) resulted in the identification of positive correlations for pathological N (HR = 2.1; p=0.009; 95% CI 1.2–3.7), pathological stage (HR = 1.4; p=0.01; 95% CI 1.0–2.0) and positive nodes (HR = 1.1; p=0.005; 95% CI 1.0–1.2).
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical analysis of clinical variables.

claim: PDAC patients with high stromal pSMAD2/3 values had significantly shorter overall survival.
source: We observed significantly shorter OS in tumor surgical samples that had high stromal pSMAD2/3 values, whether values were quantified as mean or median stromal pSMAD2/3 intensity levels (Figure 13).
evidence: The manuscript reports survival analysis results from TMA analysis.

claim: High stromal pSMAD2/3 levels also correlated with shorter recurrence-free survival in PDAC patients.
source: Even though many patients did not show clinical improvement following surgery (so that our cohort presented a bias towards fast recurrence), high stromal pSMAD2/3 levels also correlated with shorter RFS (Figure 13—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports survival analysis results from TMA analysis.

claim: Higher mean quantified levels of stromal α5β1-integrin activity correlated significantly with longer recurrence-free survival in PDAC patients.
source: In addition, higher mean quantified levels of stromal α5β1-integrin activity also correlated significantly with longer RFS (Figure 13—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript reports survival analysis results from TMA analysis.

claim: Longer times to recurrence following surgery were significantly associated with increased levels of integrin activity localized to stromal 3D-adhesion positive locations in PDAC patients.
source: Interestingly, longer times to recurrence following surgery, quantified as the percentage area coverage relative to stromal occupied areas or as integrated intensities, were significantly associated with increased levels of integrin activity localized to stromal 3D-adhesion positive locations (Figure 13—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The manuscript reports survival analysis results from TMA analysis.

claim: Stromal activation of TGFβ, represented by high stromal pSMAD2/3 levels and indicative of capacity for active production of D-ECM production, is a prognostic stromal trait for poor outcome in PDAC.
source: These results suggest that stromal activation of TGFβ, represented by high stromal pSMAD2/3 levels and indicative of capacity for active production of D-ECM production, is a prognostic stromal trait for poor outcome
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion from the survival analysis.

claim: Increased stromal levels of active α5β1-integrin at 3D adhesion positive areas may constitute a patient-protective PDAC-associated desmoplastic phenotype.
source: while increased stromal levels of active α5β1-integrin at 3D adhesion positive areas may constitute a patient-protective PDAC-associated desmoplastic phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion from the survival analysis.

claim: RCC patients with high stromal levels of pFAK-Y397 localized at 3D-adhesions, higher nuclear pSMAD2/3, or increased levels of active α5β1-integrin had significantly shorter OS and DSS.
source: Importantly, using CART analyses, we determined that RCC patients with high stromal levels of pFAK-Y397 localized at 3D-adhesions, higher nuclear pSMAD2/3, or increased levels of active α5β1-integrin, measured as mean, median or total stromal intensity levels as well as stromal percentage area coverages, had significantly shorter OS and DSS (Figure 13—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports survival analysis results for RCC patients.

claim: The markers of an active desmoplastic phenotype, as defined herein, are useful in predicting patient outcomes.
source: Together, these results strongly support the idea that the markers of an active desmoplastic phenotype, as defined herein, are useful in predicting patient outcomes.
evidence: The manuscript draws a conclusion from the survival analysis.

claim: D-ECM controls αvβ5-integrin signaling, which prompts the accumulation of activated, but FAK-independent, α5β1-integrin pools in specific intracellular vesicles.
source: We also found that D-ECM controls αvβ5-integrin signaling, which prompts the accumulation of activated, but FAK-independent, α5β1-integrin pools in specific intracellular vesicles.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes a key finding from the study.

claim: D-ECM control of αvβ5-integrin signaling prevents the enrichment of active α5β1-integrin at the plasma membrane, where α5β1 activity opposes myofibroblastic activation.
source: This D-ECM control of αvβ5-integrin signaling prevents the enrichment of active α5β1-integrin at the plasma membrane (PM), where α5β1 activity opposes myofibroblastic activation.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes a key finding from the study.

claim: Stromal localization and levels of active SMAD2/3 and α5β1-integrin distinguish patient-protective from patient-detrimental desmoplasia and foretell tumor recurrences.
source: This defined two readily distinguishable desmoplastic phenotypes that were correlated with markedly distinct clinical outcomes. These phenotypes are based on differences in the stromal localization and levels of either activated SMAD2/3 (indicative of TGFβ signaling) or active α5β1-integrin and FAK.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes the clinical significance of the findings.
